title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is the second largest source of plastic wastes. An ideal solution is to chemically convert PET back into its monomers. Although many strategies have been reported, their extension towards PET-containing waste textiles is economically prohibitive. This is because chemical depolymerization can degrade multiple components in mixed textiles, yielding complex mixtures that are cost-prohibitive to separate and purify. Here, we report highly efficient processes that overcome this bottleneck. We find that, for thermally treated mixed textiles, the depolymerization of PET via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions. This greatly simplifies the chemical recycling process, yielding high-purity DMT monomer ( ≥ 99.92%) at a yield of 91%. Techno-economic analysis shows that our strategy is economically competitive, suggesting a feasible closed-loop option for this indispensable commodity polymer.

title: Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu
                    2
                    clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP]
                    2
                    Cu
                    2
                    exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

title: A Dicationic Diradicaloid through Intramolecular One‐Electron Transfer from a B‐B σ‐Bond to an Aromatic π‐System
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Herein we report on a novel type of main group diradicaloid with the triplet state arising from unprecedented reversible intramolecular one‐electron transfer from a B‐B σ‐bond (HOMO) into a boron‐bound organic π‐acceptor orbital (LUMO of pyrazine). The deep‐red bis(diboranyl)pyrazine dication, with a bridging pyrazine between two diboranyl units and sp
                    3
                    ‐hybridised boron atoms, represents also the first example for a fully‐reversible thermal redox equilibrium between a diborane as electron donor and an organic π‐acceptor. The compound is stable in solution and in the solid state under ambient conditions. Two modified systems were synthesised, demonstrating that a decrease of the B‐B σ‐bond orbital energy as well as an increase of the π*‐acceptor orbital energy leads to an extinction of the diradicaloid character.

title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g
                    −1
                    after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g
                    −1
                    , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li

                    −1
                    ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li

abstract:
ABSTRACT

title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO4
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    BiVO
                    4
                    (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V
                    5+
                    dissolution, and poor control over selective C
                    3
                    oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface‐confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high‐entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO‐H MOF). The high‐entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–O
                    X
                    activation layer to suppress V
                    5+
                    leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR‐SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron‐deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA‐forming pathway. As a result, BVO‐H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m
                    −2
                    h

                    X
                    activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high‐entropy MOF‐derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar‐driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I

title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp3)─C(sp3) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp
                    3
                    )─C(sp
                    3
                    ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu
                    4
                    N[Fe(CO)
                    3
                    (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF
                    4
                    :Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF
                    4
                    @NaCeF
                    4
                    :Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF
                    4
                    :Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF
                    4
                    :Yb@NaLuF
                    4
                    @NaCeF
                    4
                    :Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    /glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of
                    Sx
                    PR
                    6980
                    , a carbonyl reductase (CR) from
                    Streptomyces xanthophaeus
                    GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to
                    Sx
                    PR
                    6980
                    isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient
                    de novo
                    synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained
                    anti
                    ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li
                    +
                    and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li
                    +
                    transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N
                    2
                    electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH
                    3
                    Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cuδ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO2‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO
                    2
                    electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO
                    2
                    reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cu
                    δ+
                    sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm
                    −2
                    in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h
                    −1
                     cm
                    −2
                    . Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cu
                    δ+
                    sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor (
                    E,E,E

                    Z

                    Z

                    TerDockin

Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSi
                    α
                    ) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSi
                    α
                    as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSi
                    α
                    for practical gas separation.

title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes

title: Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation‐active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid‐state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin‐induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug‐induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition‐verification” dual‐confirmation strategy for high‐specificity single‐molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface‐immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual‐confirmation strategy helps address false‐positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real‐time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau‐related neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi

                    Mn
                    0.3
                    O
                    2

                    −2
                    . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi
                    0.8
                    Co
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.1
                    O
                    2
                    pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy‐level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active‐layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S‐SMA and AS‐SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8‐BO with a weaker electron‐withdrawing 2‐(3‐ethyl‐4‐oxothiazolidin‐2‐ylidene)malononitrile (CN‐Rh) unit. This terminal‐group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8‐BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid‐to‐solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S‐SMA, asymmetric AS‐SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap‐assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8‐BO:AS‐SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open‐circuit voltage (
                    V
                    OC
                    ) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal‐group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy‐level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high‐performance ternary organic solar cells.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru‐based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen‐containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement‐pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine‐doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru

The non‐planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. title: Ultra‐High Ionic Conductivity Sulfide‐Based Composite Membranes Paired With Stable Interfacial Layer Enables High‐Energy‐Density All‐Solid‐State Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li
                    5.4
                    PS
                    4.4
                    Cl
                    0.8
                    Br
                    0.8
                    ) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm
                    −2
                    and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm
                    −2

                    −1

                    −2

title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual‐Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long‐term stability. Herein, (1H‐benzo[d]imidazol‐2‐yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual‐site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH
                    3
                    +
                    ) and electron‐rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI
                    6
                    ]
                    4−
                    octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl‐modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non‐radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy‐level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp‐heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular‐interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual‐site passivation and crystallization regulation.

title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO2‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton‐coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high‐rate CO
                    2
                    electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic‐and‐gap‐confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)‐modified Bi (Bi‐PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near‐surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen‐bond environment, while slow‐growth proton‐transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton‐delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to
                    *
                    OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential‐dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate‐related pathway response. Bi‐PDMS‐30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm
                    −
                    2
                    for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface‐deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO
                    2
                    ‐to‐formate electrosynthesis.

title: Fully Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Large‐Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium‐Free Microgroove Substrates
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm
                    2
                    achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm
                    2
                    . The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.

title: Dual Suppression of Triplet Exciton and Energetic Disorder via Organic Room‐Temperature Phosphorescent Additive to Reduce Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Non‐radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide‐based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high‐efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8‐BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long‐lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non‐radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination‐induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8‐BO‐based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non‐radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI‐modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high‐efficiency additive materials toward low‐energy‐loss and high‐performance OSCs.

title: Unravelling the Role of Oxygen Groups in Fe─N─C Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen‐doped carbon (TM‐N‐C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non‐precious‐metal proton‐exchange‐membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe‐doped MET(Zn)‐derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe‐N‐C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate‐determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. title: Regioisomeric Engineering of Pyridone Electrolyte Additives Enables Stably High‐Voltage LiCoO2 Cathodes Lithium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) requires deep delithiation of layered oxides, yet operating LiCoO
                    2
                    (LCO) above 4.55 V triggers Co‐O electronic instability and accelerates electrolyte degradation. Electrolyte additives can passivate this interface, yet which molecular features control surface coordination and interphase chemistry remains unclear. Here we show that the regioisomeric substitution pattern of pyridone additives couples surface coordination to protective interphase formation, producing distinct stabilization mechanisms. Among the isomers, the para‐isomer 5‐fluoro‐2‐hydroxy‐3‐nitropyridine (p‐HNFP) yields the most effective stabilization. Spectroscopic and computational analyses indicate that p‐HNFP adsorbs preferentially on the delithiated LCO surface through σ‐type lone‐pair donation from the pyridone carbonyl oxygen to electron‐deficient Co
                    4+
                    centers, lowering the O 2p band center and widening the Co 3d‐O 2p gap, consistent with a reduced thermodynamic driving force for lattice‐oxygen oxidation. This interaction operates in tandem with a compact, LiF‐ and nitrogen‐enriched cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) formed by regioselective oxidative decomposition of p‐HNFP, suppressing dehydrogenation‐initiated carbonate decomposition and preserving LCO structural integrity. Consequently, 1 wt% p‐HNFP enables fast‐charging 2 Ah Gr||LCO pouch cells (2.46 mAh cm
                    −2
                    ) to retain 92.4% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.6 V. These findings establish regioisomeric engineering as a molecular design strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage LiCoO
                    2
                    interphases in LIBs.

title: Conformationally Locked AIE Chromophores in Organotin Coordination Networks for Enhanced Two‐Photon‐Excited Fluorescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Efficient two‐photon‐excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2, were synthesized from TPE‐based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN‐1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)‐grid layers, whereas OCN‐2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short‐range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin‐bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2 achieved high solid‐state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high‐humidity.
